title: The Prognostic Value of Immune Factors in the Tumor Microenvironment of Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: retrospective observational cohort study with immunohistochemistry on whole-mount sections and tissue microarray
country_setting: Netherlands; single centre (Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam)
funding: NR
conflicts_of_interest: None declared; authors state the research was conducted without commercial or financial relationships
population_description: Consecutive patients with invasive penile SCC surgically treated at a single Dutch centre 2001-2009; median age 65.9 years; 61.0% pT2; 68 (31.9%) with lymph node metastases; median follow-up 100.7 months
hpv_method: GP5+/6+ PCR enzyme-immunoassay for 14 HPV types
time_markers: PD-L1, CD8, FOXP3, CD163, CD68, HLA
primary_aim_as_stated: To identify immunological prognosticators for lymph node metastases and disease-specific survival in penile SCC, and to identify associations between tumour microenvironment factors and those outcomes
key_finding_time: CD8 and FoxP3 counts were markedly higher in stromal than in tumour areas in both hrHPV subgroups. Double staining of 12 cases showed most macrophages were CD68+CD163+ in both compartments, indicating near-universal M2 polarisation
key_finding_hpv: PD-L1 was the only immune factor differing by HPV status: hrHPV-negative tumours were positive more often (49.4% vs 32.7%, P=0.03). No differences in classical or non-classical HLA, CD8, FoxP3 or CD163 infiltration between subgroups
key_finding_prognosis: In the multivariable model diffuse PD-L1 tumour-cell expression was the only immune factor still associated with LNM (OR 2.81, 95% CI 1.01-7.81, P=0.05). hrHPV negativity (HR 9.73, P<0.01) and diffuse PD-L1 (HR 2.78, P=0.03) both predicted poor disease-specific survival. Univariably, high intratumoural CD163 (OR 2.45) and non-classical HLA upregulation (OR 2.28) were also linked to LNM
limitations_as_stated: Few cases with LNM and disease-related deaths limited statistical power; substantial missing HLA data because of insufficient TMA tissue; PD-1 expression, distance between CD8 T-cells and PD-L1-expressing cells, and functionality were not assessed; external validation needed
other_key_outcomes: HPV16 was the predominant type among hrHPV-positive tumours (41/52, 79%). Well-differentiated tumours were overwhelmingly hrHPV-negative (70 vs 9), yet hrHPV-positive patients still had better survival (2 vs 27 penile-cancer deaths, log-rank P=0.02)
extraction_note: N=213 is the analytic cohort for the whole-mount IHC (PD-L1, CD8, FoxP3, CD163); HLA class I was assessed on a TMA of only 168 samples and hrHPV typing on 212, so denominators differ by marker. hpv_positive_pct=24.8 uses 52/210 (Table 1 states three cases with unknown hrHPV status), but Methods report hrHPV typing on 212 samples; the two figures cannot both be right and the paper does not reconcile them. CD68 was stained only in 12 selected cases by immunofluorescence, not across the cohort. No funding statement appears anywhere in the article. No immunotherapy was administered. Same NKI 2001-2009 series from which ref 13 (Rafael 2021) draws its 103 cases, so the two are not independent cohorts

title: Immunophenotypes Based on the Tumor Immune Microenvironment Allow for Unsupervised Penile Cancer Patient Stratification.
study_design: retrospective single-centre cohort with immunohistochemistry of nine immune markers and unsupervised hierarchical clustering
country_setting: China; single centre (Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou)
funding: Nature Science Foundation of China (81872085, 81872266); Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities (19ykpy178); Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province (2019A1515010197); SYSUCC Medical Scientist Training Program (14zxqk08)
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declare no conflict of interest
population_description: 178 consecutive patients with invasive penile SCC admitted January 1999-December 2013; median age 52 (range 24-86); 75 (42.1%) with lymph node metastasis; median follow-up 88 months; 44 deaths from penile SCC
hpv_method: Real-time PCR (Hybribio HybriMax assay) detecting 23 HPV types, including 13 high-risk types
time_markers: PD-L1, PD-1, CTLA-4, CD8, FOXP3, CD68, TAM, other_checkpoint, other_immune
primary_aim_as_stated: To determine the immunophenotype of the tumour immune microenvironment in penile SCC by integrating expression of immune checkpoints and tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte components, and to analyse the relationship between the microenvironment and hrHPV and the clinical significance of the immunophenotypes
key_finding_time: Unsupervised clustering of 163 patients yielded four immunophenotypes: A immune ignorance / cold (30, 18.4%), B immune inflammatory (24, 14.7%), C immune exclusion (27, 16.6%), D immune tolerance (82, 50.3%). Fifteen patients could not be clustered because of missing values
key_finding_hpv: No significant difference in hrHPV infection across the four immunophenotypes. hrHPV-positive tumours showed higher stromal Granzyme B and intratumoral PD-1 density (p=0.049 and p=0.002); PD-L1 and Siglec-15 expression were unrelated to hrHPV status
key_finding_prognosis: Diffuse PD-L1 tumour-cell expression carried worse prognosis than marginal expression (HR 3.055, p=0.004). Immunophenotype was an independent prognostic factor for DSS (clusters A and C vs B and D, HR 2.349, p=0.014) and an independent predictor of LNM (OR 2.482, p=0.037). High densities of GrB, FOXP3, CD68, CD206, PD-1 and CTLA-4 were each associated with better DSS
limitations_as_stated: Single-centre retrospective design; some immunohistochemistry unavailable because of insufficient tissue; CD68 and CD206 used as macrophage markers instead of alternatives such as CD163, which may alter results; no uniform standard for immune-marker cut-offs, so DSS-derived cut-points were used; multiplex immunofluorescence was not performed on all samples; external validation needed
other_key_outcomes: HPV16 was the predominant type among hrHPV-positive tumours (54/58). Adding immunophenotype to a model with T stage, N stage and hrHPV raised the c-statistic from 0.861 to 0.875
extraction_note: N=178 is the cohort with immunohistochemistry; the unsupervised clustering that defines the four immunophenotypes rests on 163 patients (15 excluded for missing values), and marker-specific denominators differ (e.g. Siglec-15 scored in 170). Denominators also shift between subtables: Table 1 grade percentages are computed on 173 and T-stage percentages on 174, without explanation. Macrophages were assessed with CD68 and CD206, not CD163. Granzyme B mapped to other_immune, CD206 to TAM and Siglec-15 to other_checkpoint, as none has its own token in the codebook

title: Interplay of PD-L1, FOXP3, and CD8 in the Immune Microenvironment of Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Expression Profiles and Correlations.
study_design: cross-sectional retrospective translational study using tissue microarrays (4 TMAs, 528 spots from 108 patients) with immunohistochemistry for PD-L1, FOXP3 and CD8; spot-level Spearman correlations and Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn's post-hoc tests against histological grade, HPV-associated morphology and host inflammatory response; no clinical outcome/survival analysis
country_setting: NR
funding: None; the authors state they received no financial support for the research, authorship, or publication of this article
conflicts_of_interest: None declared (authors state no potential conflicts of interest regarding the research, authorship, or publication of this article)
population_description: 108 patients with invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the penis; specimens selected by availability of FFPE tissue blocks (1-4 blocks/specimen); 4 TMAs constructed, 3 cores/block, yielding 528 evaluable spots; no age, stage, or follow-up data reported; analysis conducted predominantly at the spot level rather than the patient level
primary_aim_as_stated: To conduct a comprehensive examination of the expression profiles and correlations between PD-L1, FOXP3+ regulatory T cells, and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells within tumor and stromal compartments of penile SCC, characterizing the immune landscape and its associations with histological grade, HPV-associated morphology, and host inflammatory response
key_finding_time: PD-L1 in tumor cells correlated positively with PD-L1 in lymphocytes (rho=0.475), intratumoral FOXP3+ (rho=0.293) and CD8+ (rho=0.408), and peritumoral FOXP3+ (rho=0.333) and CD8+ (rho=0.251); peritumoral FOXP3+ and CD8+ showed the strongest correlation of all (rho=0.753); PD-L1 (tumor and lymphocyte) and intratumoral CD8+ increased significantly with higher histological grade, while FOXP3+ infiltration did not vary significantly by grade; more intense host inflammatory response was associated with higher peritumoral FOXP3+ and higher intratumoral and peritumoral CD8+ densities
key_finding_hpv: HPV-associated morphology (WHO 2022 histologic criteria, not molecular testing) was associated with higher PD-L1 expression in tumor cells (median 10% vs 1%, P<.001) but lower FOXP3+ infiltration in both intratumoral (median 2 vs 6.5 cells/HPF, P=.002) and peritumoral (median 22.5 vs 57.5 cells/HPF, P<.001) compartments; CD8+ infiltration and lymphocytic PD-L1 expression did not differ significantly by HPV-associated morphology
key_finding_prognosis: NA
limitations_as_stated: Tissue microarrays may not fully capture whole-tumor heterogeneity; cross-sectional design precludes assessment of the temporal evolution of the immune response; HPV status was inferred morphologically rather than by direct molecular testing; PD-L1 was assessed with a research-use antibody (clone E1L3N) and a broad >0% positivity threshold rather than a clinically validated companion-diagnostic assay/cut-off, limiting translational comparability
other_key_outcomes: PD-L1 expression in tumor cells varied significantly by histological subtype (Kruskal-Wallis H=77.26, P<.001): papillary subtype lowest (median 0%) vs basaloid (25%) and warty-basaloid (20%); all 3 sarcomatoid spots showed 100% PD-L1, all 7 verrucous spots showed 0%. Full dataset and analysis scripts made openly available (Figshare and GitHub).
extraction_note: Spot-level study, not patient-level: n_patients=108 is the number of patients contributing FFPE blocks, but nearly all quantitative results (Spearman correlations, Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn comparisons) are computed across TMA spots (up to 528), with markedly uneven marker-specific evaluable-spot denominators (e.g. FOXP3 quantified in only 80 spots vs 504-506 for PD-L1/CD8), and the reason for the much larger data loss specific to FOXP3 scoring is not explained in the text -- flagging possible attrition/selection bias concentrated in the FOXP3 findings. No patient-level demographic (age, stage) or follow-up/survival data are reported anywhere in the article, so key_finding_prognosis=NA and key_finding_immunotherapy=NA (no immunotherapy was administered; this is a correlative IHC study only). country_setting recorded as NR: Methods do not state where the 108 specimens originated; IRB approval was obtained from Johns Hopkins School of Medicine (Baltimore, MD, USA), but author affiliations include Instituto de Patologia e Investigacion (Asuncion, Paraguay) and the corresponding author is Paraguay-based; the article's own reference list includes Chaux et al. 2013 (World J Urol), describing a Paraguayan cohort of 103 penile-carcinoma patients, raising the possibility of an overlapping or identical Paraguayan specimen archive, but this is not stated explicitly in the Methods and is not recorded as fact -- needs reconciliation with R1. hpv_stratified=partial and hpv_method=NR because HPV status here is not molecular (no p16/PCR/ISH) but inferred purely from histologic subtype per WHO 2022 criteria ('HPV-associated' vs 'HPV-independent' morphology); the authors themselves flag this as a limitation and call for direct molecular HPV testing in future work. hpv_positive_pct=NR: the article reports spot-level group comparisons by HPV-associated vs HPV-independent morphology but never states an overall percentage of HPV-associated patients or spots. Statistical caveat not captured elsewhere in the codebook: Spearman/Kruskal-Wallis tests treat spots as independent observations despite multiple correlated spots per patient (3-12 spots/patient), with no clustering-adjusted (e.g. mixed-effects) analysis reported, which may inflate the apparent significance of the reported correlations and group comparisons. Note for reconciliation: this is the reference with the review's own conflict of interest (Chaux is a co-author), which is why an extractor without that conflict was assigned to this row; the primary study's own COI/funding declarations are clean and unrelated to that meta-level conflict.

title: Distinct Patterns of Myeloid Cell Infiltration in Patients With hrHPV-Positive and hrHPV-Negative Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma: The Importance of Assessing Myeloid Cell Densities Within the Spatial Context of the Tumor.
study_design: retrospective hypothesis-generating cohort study with digital image analysis of immunohistochemistry across four annotated spatial compartments
country_setting: Netherlands; single centre (Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam)
funding: NR
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declare the research was conducted without commercial or financial relationships
population_description: Patients surgically treated for penile carcinoma 2001-2009 at a single Dutch centre, drawn from a previously described cohort of 213 (52 hrHPV-positive, 158 hrHPV-negative); selection required histologically confirmed invasive penile carcinoma and adequate tissue; hrHPV-negative cases were chosen to profile against the original cohort by pT stage and cause of death; median age 66.9
hpv_method: GP5+/6+ PCR enzyme immunoassay for 14 hrHPV subtypes
primary_aim_as_stated: To annotate penile SCC resection specimens into spatial compartments, quantify CD14+, CD68+ and CD163+ myeloid cells within them using image analysis, and assess their association with clinical parameters including HPV status and patient survival
key_finding_time: Stromal compartments held higher myeloid densities than tumoral ones for all three markers. In stroma, CD68+ cells were less numerous than CD14+ and CD163+ (medians 311.4, 1047.1 and 1163.6 cells/mm2), whereas tumour-compartment densities were comparable (97.3, 171.4, 132.4)
key_finding_hpv: hrHPV-positive tumours had significantly higher CD14+, CD68+ and CD163+ densities in the intratumoral tumour compartment (all p<0.001); this was absent in intratumoral stroma (p=0.57, 0.08, 0.68). In the peritumoral tumour compartment CD14+ and CD68+ also differed (p=0.004, p=0.026). Differences between hrHPV subgroups were driven mainly by the intratumoral tumour compartment
key_finding_prognosis: Risk of penile-cancer death fell slightly as intratumoral tumour myeloid density rose (CD14 sHR 0.997, p=0.04; CD68 sHR 0.995, p=0.05; CD163 sHR 0.995, p=0.02), but no association survived adjustment for hrHPV status (p=0.65, 0.96, 0.53). In the hrHPV-positive subgroup, high CD68+ and CD163+ in the peritumoral tumour compartment were associated with lymph node metastasis (p=0.031, p=0.026)
limitations_as_stated: The immunohistochemistry methodology did not allow identification of myeloid cell subsets; no correction for multiple testing was applied, deliberately, to avoid type II errors; the study is hypothesis-generating and needs confirmation in another cohort; only one hrHPV-positive patient died of penile cancer, making risk analysis impossible in that subgroup
other_key_outcomes: Myeloid densities in tumoral compartments rose with differentiation grade (CD14 p=0.001; CD68 and CD163 p<0.001), and this persisted in the hrHPV-negative subgroup analysed alone. hrHPV status itself had a significant favourable effect on survival (sHR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.89, p=0.038)
extraction_note: The text states 43 (33%) hrHPV-positive and 60 (58%) hrHPV-negative of 103; 43/103 is 41.7%, so the 33% figure is arithmetically wrong and is probably a carry-over from the parent cohort (52/213 = 24%). hpv_positive_pct recorded as 41.7 from the counts, not from the stated percentage. N=103 is the image-analysis cohort; hierarchical clustering used only 90 (13 excluded for missing values). This cohort is a selected subset of the same NKI 2001-2009 series reported in ref 10 (Ottenhof 2018), cited here as reference 27, so the two are not independent. CD14 mapped to other_immune as it has no token in the codebook. No funding statement appears anywhere in the article

title: Geospatial and Cell Density Analysis Using Multiplex Immunofluorescence Reveals an Important Role of Clustering Patterns of Immunosuppressive Macrophages in Survival Outcomes of Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
study_design: retrospective cohort with multiplex immunofluorescence on a tissue microarray and geospatial point-pattern analysis
country_setting: United States; single centre (H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center, Tampa, Florida)
funding: None; the article states the research received no external funding
conflicts_of_interest: J.C. reports advisory board or consultancy fees from Merck, Pfizer, Exelixis, Aveo, Eisai and Mycaregorythm; institutional research funding from ten companies; co-founder of AI-OS LLC; editor for PDQ NCI. P.E.S. reports honoraria from UpToDate. All other authors declare none
population_description: 57 men with invasive penile SCC treated 2010-2016; median age 60 (range 31-92); mostly Caucasian (77%); all had clinically node-positive disease or high-risk primary tumours and all underwent inguinal lymph node dissection; 31/57 (54%) pathologically node-positive; all samples from primary tumour resections
hpv_method: p16 IHC, with high-risk HPV testing by Cobas HPV assay (Roche) on all p16-positive samples; Tables 1 and 3 instead label HPV status as ISH
time_markers: PD-L1, CD8, CD68, CD163, FOXP3, TAM, other_immune
primary_aim_as_stated: To characterise immune cell density and geospatial clustering patterns within the tumour immune microenvironment of penile SCC and to evaluate their associations with clinical outcomes
key_finding_time: Median densities were higher in stroma than tumour for every phenotype. M1 macrophage median density (157.64 cells/mm2) exceeded the combined M2 medians (58.79 CD68+CD163+ and 48.09 CD68+CD206+). Cytotoxic and helper T cells were sparse (10.11 and 12.20) relative to memory T cells (519.24)
key_finding_hpv: HPV-negative status predicted worse OS (HR 0.34 for HPV-positive, p=0.034 univariably; HR 2.9, 95% CI 1.1-8.3 for HPV-negative). T lymphocyte density did not differ by HPV status, and among patients with high bivariate clustering of CD3+CD4+ cells with tumour cells OS did not differ by HPV status, suggesting an HPV-agnostic biomarker
key_finding_prognosis: High M1 macrophage density improved OS (91 vs 28 months, p<0.005). Intratumoral clustering of M2 macrophages with tumour cells predicted worse OS (19 months vs not reached, p=0.011), worse RFS (HR 2.94, 95% CI 1.24-6.96) and worse CSS (HR 3.77, 95% CI 1.2-11.3). Stromal self-clustering of M2 macrophages also worsened OS (28 vs 96 months, p=0.02). High intratumoral CD3+CD4+ density improved OS (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.154-0.938). Nodal stage pN2-3 carried HR 7.70 (2.58-22.96)
limitations_as_stated: PD-L1 was evaluated at tissue-microarray rather than cellular level, limiting study of immune-exhaustion patterns; all samples were primary tumour resections, precluding analysis of resected nodal tissue or treatment-specific signatures; limited racial diversity prevented race-stratified analyses; relatively small cohort
other_key_outcomes: 45.6% recurred, mostly inguino-pelvic (local 5, regional 15, distant 6); median time to recurrence 6.3 months; median OS 36.3 months; median follow-up 45.5 months. PD-L1 status, adjuvant therapy, T stage and lymphovascular invasion were not associated with OS
extraction_note: HPV method conflicts within the paper: Methods describe p16 IHC followed by Cobas PCR, but Tables 1 and 3 label HPV status as ISH. Recorded from Methods. Adjuvant therapy is 17/57 (30%) per the text and Table 3; Table 2 instead reports Yes 26 (45.6%) / No 21 (36.8%), figures copied verbatim from the recurrence and vital-status rows above and summing to 47, so Table 2 is the erroneous one. Table 3 LVI counts sum to 55 of 57 with no missing-data row. The PD-L1 hazard ratio in Table 3 (1.23, 95% CI 0.78-3.39) is internally inconsistent, though not significant either way. The geospatial clustering radius is given as 50 nanometres, presumably a units error for micrometres. CD206 mapped to TAM and Granzyme-type / NKp46 / CD45RO markers to other_immune, as they have no tokens in the codebook

title: A B cell-IgA-epithelial axis enhances antitumor immunity and improves outcome in HPV-associated penile squamous cell carcinoma.
study_design: observational translational study: scRNA-seq discovery cohort (23 tumors, 5 normal adjacent tissues) plus FFPE validation cohort assessed by IHC, multiplex immunofluorescence, flow cytometry and ELISA, with in vitro and mouse functional experiments
country_setting: China; single centre (First Affiliated Hospital, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei)
funding: Key R&D Program of MOST (2023YFC2306203, 2023YFC2306101); CAS Strategic Priority Research Program (XDB0490000); CAS Project for Young Scientists in Basic Research (YSBR-074); NSFC 32170912 and 82371828; Anhui provincial grants; USTC Major Joint Project of New Medicine
conflicts_of_interest: None declared (authors state no competing interests)
population_description: Treatment-naive PSCC patients undergoing surgical excision; scRNA-seq discovery cohort of 23 tumours (13 HPV-negative, 10 HPV-positive) and 5 normal adjacent tissues; validation cohort of 85 FFPE cases (52 HPV-negative, 33 HPV-positive) for IHC and multiplex immunofluorescence; 20 fresh tumours for flow cytometry; 16 for bulk BCR-seq; 13 for ELISA
hpv_method: p16 IHC (strong diffuse staining in at least 70% of tumour cells) plus HPV PCR with SPF1/GP6++ primers; HPV16/18 DNA in situ hybridisation additionally in the discovery cohort
primary_aim_as_stated: To apply single-cell RNA sequencing to explore the heterogeneity and differences of the tumour microenvironment in HPV-positive versus HPV-negative PSCC, and to identify key immune cell populations and their roles within it
key_finding_time: Immune cells were the dominant TME compartment in PSCC (74.62%), higher than in HNSCC, cSCC and NPC; CD4, CD8, CD20, CD86 and CD56 cells per area were all increased in tumour versus adjacent normal tissue; among immune subsets only tumour-infiltrating B cells and tertiary lymphoid structures differed by HPV status
key_finding_hpv: HPV-positive tumours showed higher tumour-infiltrating B cells (P=0.0007 by scRNA-seq, P=0.0151 by flow cytometry), higher TLS density per tumour area (P=0.0029), more CD20+ B cells and CD38+ plasma cells within TLSs, and higher IHC scores for CD138 (28/33 vs 14/52 with score >=3), IgA (26/33 vs 2/52), PIGR (29/33 vs 1/52) and IFN-gamma (21/28 vs 2/28); CD3+ T cells within TLSs and IgG did not differ
key_finding_prognosis: HPV-positive patients had better overall survival than HPV-negative (n=85, P=0.0136); high IgA IHC score (>=3) was associated with better survival (P=0.0209) whereas IgG and CD138 were not; high PIGR was associated with better survival (P=0.0236); combined high PIGR and high IgA showed the best survival (P=0.0382)
limitations_as_stated: No dedicated limitations section; authors note that the MC38 mouse model has low B-cell and plasma-cell infiltration and that IgA there is likely peripherally sourced, that tissue allocation to assays was dictated by real-time availability and IHC was run only once per sample because of limited biospecimen, and that whether the antibodies produced in HPV-positive tumours are tumour-reactive or directed against viral antigens remains unresolved
other_key_outcomes: Functional validation: PIGR overexpression in PSCC primary cells reduced proliferation, colony formation and migration and increased apoptosis under IgA stimulation, and slowed xenograft growth in nude mice; PIGR-driven tumour control was lost after anti-CD20 B-cell depletion and in IgA-deficient mice in the MC38 model, with reduced IFN-gamma+, TNF-alpha+ and GZMB+ CD8 T-cell infiltration; IFN-gamma was the strongest inducer of PIGR expression in vitro; in TCGA data high PIGR plus high IgA correlated with better survival in cervical, head and neck and colon carcinoma but not in bladder, breast, oesophageal or lung cancer. Authors frame the IgA-PIGR axis as a possible biomarker and therapeutic angle beyond T-cell-directed immunotherapy
extraction_note: n_patients ambiguous: 107 PSCC cases in total, 23 tumours in the scRNA-seq discovery cohort, 85 evaluable FFPE cases in the IHC and survival validation cohort (5 archival cases excluded for discordant p16-positive/PCR-negative results), 20 fresh tumours for flow cytometry, 16 for bulk BCR-seq, 13 for ELISA, 37 slides for the intra-tumour versus non-tumour TLS comparison. 85 recorded as the analytic N because all IHC quantification and all survival analyses rest on it; hpv_positive_pct=38.8 refers to that cohort (33/85), while in the scRNA-seq cohort it is 10/23 (43.5%). No immunotherapy was administered to patients, so key_finding_immunotherapy=NA and the preclinical IgA-PIGR results are recorded under other_key_outcomes. Published online 11 December 2025, issue dated 2026.

title: A model of tertiary lymphatic structure-related prognosis for penile squamous cell carcinoma.
study_design: retrospective two-centre cohort with H&E-based tertiary lymphoid structure density scoring, Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analysis and a prognostic nomogram
country_setting: China; two centres (Guangxi Medical University Cancer Hospital and Wuming Hospital, Nanning, Guangxi)
funding: National Natural Science Fund of China (32260241, 82360587); Guangxi Natural Science Foundation (2024GXNSFDA010022, 2023GXNSFDA026021); Guangxi medical and health technology development projects; Guangxi 139 plan for high-level talents (G201903036)
conflicts_of_interest: None declared (authors state no competing interests)
population_description: 83 patients with penile squamous cell carcinoma, AJCC 2017 stage I to IV, treated between June 2013 and April 2023; 57 with and 26 without TLS on histopathological sections; median follow-up 37 months (range 1-118) with 14 deaths; mean age approximately 52-55 years; patients with non-squamous penile tumours, concurrent second malignancies or missing clinical data were excluded
primary_aim_as_stated: To clarify the relationship between tertiary lymphoid structures and penile squamous cell carcinoma and to provide a theoretical basis for the treatment of penile cancer
key_finding_time: TLSs were identified on H&E in 57/83 cases (68.7%) and were absent in 26/83; TLS density was scored on H&E alone without immune markers; TLS status was associated with APTT (P=0.046), D-dimer (P=0.034), reported life cycle (P=0.018) and squamous cell carcinoma antigen (P=0.049) but not with T, N, M, grade, tumour volume or recurrence
key_finding_hpv: NA
key_finding_prognosis: In multivariate Cox analysis TLS (HR 0.077, 95% CI 0.015-0.411, P=0.003), BMI (HR 0.786, P=0.010), T stage (HR 3.861, P=0.004), N stage (HR 2.051, P=0.002) and M stage (HR 0.042, P=0.002) were independent predictors of overall survival; the BMI/T/N/M/TLS nomogram reached a C-index of 0.884 (0.835-0.932) and the one-year decision curve 0.581 (0.508-0.655). In subgroup analyses the direction reversed: among node-positive T3 patients and among patients with perineural invasion without distant spread, prognosis was better without TLS (P=0.026 and P=0.032)
limitations_as_stated: TLS presence and number were judged on H&E by two pathologists without CD3, CD20 or other immune markers, so the assessment carried a degree of subjectivity; the mechanism underlying the survival differences by TLS status remains unclear
other_key_outcomes: TLS number correlated inversely with survival time (R=-0.216, P=0.018) and the survival time distribution differed by TLS status (P=0.02 and P=0.018), while the Kaplan-Meier curve of overall survival with versus without TLS was not significant (P=0.498); the authors attribute the longer mean survival without TLS to the imbalance of T3/T4 cases (21 with TLS versus 11 without). PLR was also analysed (AUC 0.753, 95% CI 0.608-0.897; Kaplan-Meier P=0.005 with TLS and P=0.004 without)
extraction_note: Internal inconsistencies in the source, recorded as printed and not reconciled: (1) TLS is reported as a significant independent predictor (HR 0.077, P=0.003, Fig 3A and Results) but does not appear in Table 3, and the Kaplan-Meier comparison of overall survival with versus without TLS is non-significant (P=0.498, Table 2 and Fig 4B), while the Discussion states that mean survival was longer without TLS; (2) Table 2 lists M0 n=2 and M1 n=55, the reverse of Table 1 (M1 n=2, M0 n=55); (3) N-side percentages in Table 1 sum inconsistently (61.6% versus 61.5%). No HPV testing was performed, so hpv_stratified=no and all HPV fields are NR. PLR has no controlled token and was therefore left out of time_markers and recorded under other_key_outcomes; it could alternatively be coded as other_immune.

title: Classic and nonclassic HLA class I expression in penile cancer and relation to HPV status and clinical outcome.
study_design: retrospective cohort with tissue microarray immunohistochemistry, Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analysis
country_setting: The Netherlands; single-institution cohort (Department of Pathology, The Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam), with immunostaining scored at VU University Medical Center
funding: NR
conflicts_of_interest: NR
population_description: 168 patients with penile cancer who underwent surgical excision at a single institution between 2000 and 2009, selected on the availability of sufficient material for tissue microarray construction (185 blocks retrieved, 17 excluded for insufficient representative tumour); mean age 65 years (range 28-96); median follow-up 62 months (IQR 56-72); lymph node positivity in 55 patients (33%); no preoperative radiotherapy or chemotherapy; 141 cases were of the squamous subtype; at last follow-up 124 alive, 22 dead of penile carcinoma and 22 of other causes
primary_aim_as_stated: To analyse the expression of classic and nonclassic HLA class I in a large penile cancer cohort in relation to clinicopathological parameters, HPV status and clinical outcome
key_finding_time: Complete and partial loss of total classic HLA class I was observed in 32% and 50% of cases and up-regulation of HLA-E and HLA-G in 16% and 13%; in the 141 squamous-subtype cases the corresponding figures were 21% complete loss, 40% partial loss, 18% HLA-E and 12% HLA-G up-regulation. Positive expression of HLA-A, HLA-B/C and total classic HLA class I was more frequent in pT3-4 than in pT1-2 tumours (P=0.01, 0.02 and <0.01) and HLA-E up-regulation was more common in patients with tumour-positive lymph nodes (P=0.01)
key_finding_hpv: No difference in HLA-A, HLA-B/C, HLA-E or HLA-G expression between HPV-positive and HPV-negative cases (P=0.26 to 0.59). Survival associations differed by HPV status: in HPV-negative tumours 5-year disease-specific survival differed across positive, weak and negative HLA-A expression (93%, 68% and 84%, P=0.02) and weak total classic HLA class I was linked to worse survival than negative expression (P=0.02), whereas no HLA subgroup was prognostic among HPV-positive tumours. High-risk HPV positivity was itself associated with better survival (univariable HR 0.1, 95% CI 0.0-0.8, P=0.03)
key_finding_prognosis: Weak HLA-A expression was an independent predictor of decreased 5-year disease-specific survival overall (HR 2.3, 95% CI 1.1-4.6, P=0.02) and in HPV-negative patients (HR 3.4, 95% CI 1.4-8.4, P<0.01) after adjustment for lymph node status, pT stage, differentiation grade, LVI and high-risk HPV; total classic HLA class I was not independently significant (HR 1.9, 95% CI 0.8-4.2, P=0.13) and HLA-B/C, HLA-E and HLA-G were not associated with survival; no differences in disease-free survival were found for any subtype
limitations_as_stated: Only tissue from patients not pretreated with chemotherapy was used, so patients with advanced tumours are under-represented; despite the cohort size and length of follow-up relatively few events occurred, which may have influenced the results
other_key_outcomes: Staining was scored semiquantitatively with the Ruiter quality-control system by a single experienced observer, on 3 cores of 0.6 mm per case with at least 2 evaluable cores required; classic HLA class I was graded as positive (score 7-8), weak (3-6) or negative (0-2) and HLA-E and HLA-G were scored in binary fashion on tumour cells, with resident leukocytes and vessel endothelium as internal positive controls
extraction_note: hpv_method not determinable from this report: HPV status was carried over from a previous study of the same cohort (reference 11) and no assay is described here, so it is recorded as NR rather than inferred; the keywords cite a human papillomavirus DNA test. time_compartment is ambiguous: Methods state that scoring used the intensity and percent of positive cells in the tumour and in stromal cells surrounding the tumour, but the score categories and the binary HLA-E/G scoring are defined on tumour cells and infiltrating immune and stromal cells are described as positive controls; recorded as tumor. hpv_positive_pct=29 is as stated (48 patients, 48/165 with known HPV status = 29.1%). Table 1 denominators are inconsistent between rows: classic HLA percentages exclude cases with unknown status from failed TMA staining (up to n=45) while HLA-E and HLA-G percentages appear to be calculated over the full 168. No funding statement and no conflict of interest declaration appear in the article.

title: The peri- and intratumoral immune cell infiltrate and PD-L1 status in invasive squamous cell carcinomas of the penis.
study_design: retrospective single-centre cohort with semiquantitative H&E-based immune cell infiltrate scoring and PD-L1 immunohistochemistry in a subset, analysed by Fisher exact test, Kaplan-Meier, log-rank and Cox regression
country_setting: Germany; single centre (Dr. Senckenberg Institute of Pathology, University Hospital Frankfurt am Main; samples provided by the University Cancer Center Frankfurt)
funding: Dr. Senckenberg Institute of Pathology, Frankfurt am Main; open access funding enabled and organised by Projekt DEAL
conflicts_of_interest: PJW reports consulting fees and honoraria for lectures from Bayer, Janssen-Cilag, Novartis, Roche, MSD, Astellas Pharma, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Molecular Health, Sophia Genetics, Qiagen and AstraZeneca; all other authors declare no conflict of interest
population_description: 60 invasive penile squamous cell carcinomas identified in the institutional archive, treated by partial penectomy with or without lymphadenectomy; age range 41-85 years (55% aged 65 or less); pT1a 38%, pT1b 12%, pT2 38%, pT3 5%, pT4 3%, pTX 3%; nodal status pN0 22%, pN positive 15%, pNX 63%; G2 in 65%; usual type 90% and basaloid 10%; clinical follow-up available for all patients; PD-L1 was stained in the 30 tumours with sufficient material
hpv_method: HPV DNA genotyping with the HPV 3.5 LCD-Array kit (Chipron) on macrodissected paraffin sections, plus p16 immunohistochemistry (CINtec Histology, Roche; block-like positivity scored positive and mosaic pattern negative)
primary_aim_as_stated: Assuming that HPV infection leads to an exaggerated immune cell response by the host, to investigate the peri- and intratumoral immune cell infiltrate in invasive penile squamous cell carcinomas and to correlate it with the known survival data of the cohort
key_finding_time: Immune cell infiltrate scored on H&E was low in 4/60 (7%), medium in 24/60 (40%) and high in 32/60 (53%). In the 30 tumours stained for PD-L1, mean TPS was 18% (range 0-90, SD 26) with staining above 0% in 26/30 (87%); median IC was 12% (range 0-50, SD 13) and IC above 0% was present in 28/30 (93%) according to Table 1 and the abstract; mean CPS was 29 (range 0-100, SD 36) with CPS above 0 in 29/30 (97%). Immune cell infiltrate was significantly associated with pT stage (P=0.0426), PD-L1 IC (P=0.0017) and CPS (P=0.0382) but not with TPS (P=0.1193)
key_finding_hpv: No association between immune cell infiltrate and HPV status by LCD-array (P=0.3736) or p16 immunohistochemistry (P=0.4307), and neither HPV status (P=0.374, relative hazard 0.607) nor p16 (P=0.409) was associated with overall survival; the authors conclude that in their cohort factors other than HPV drive the increased immune cell infiltrate
key_finding_prognosis: Immune cell infiltrate and pT stage were prognostic for overall survival: univariable low or median versus high infiltrate P=0.024 with relative hazard 3.876 (95% CI 1.171-12.83) and pT stage P=0.000; in the model with dichotomised variables ICI had HR 0.108 (0.013-0.912, P=0.041), pT stage HR 7.489 (1.458-38.468, P=0.016) and the pT by ICI interaction HR 59.69 (1.668-2136.074, P=0.025). PD-L1 TPS, IC and CPS were not associated with overall survival
limitations_as_stated: Comparison with other PD-L1 studies is limited by the use of different antibodies and different positivity cut-offs (5% versus 1%) and by the small number of investigated samples; the association between IC or CPS and immune cell infiltrate may reflect a scoring bias, since a larger amount of lymphocytes is likely scored as higher IC and consequently higher CPS; the cohort needs to be enlarged to cover low tumour stages and multicentre data are needed; uniform criteria and cut-off values are lacking for the invasive front
other_key_outcomes: No significant differences in immune cell infiltrate by nodal status, grading, infiltration pattern or morphological tumour type. Immunohistochemical markers were deliberately not used for the infiltrate so that the assessment would be reproducible for pathologists regardless of their immunohistochemical repertoire; PD-L1 was stained with clone ZR3 at 1:200 on slides with more than 100 tumour cells and scored by two surgical pathologists without knowledge of clinical data. The authors conclude that PD-L1 expression provides a rationale for checkpoint inhibitor therapy and that routine PD-L1 testing should be performed in invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma for potential off-label use
extraction_note: n_patients=60 is the analytic N for the immune cell infiltrate and survival analyses (data available for all 60); PD-L1 was assessed only in the 30 tumours with sufficient material, so all PD-L1 figures have a denominator of 30. Discrepancy within the source: the Results text states positive IC (above 0%) in 25/30 (83%), whereas Table 1 (IC 0% in 2/30) and the abstract give 28/30 (93%); recorded as 93% with the discrepancy noted. Table 3 also reports CPS with relative hazard 2.773 and 95% CI 0.278-2.764, a point estimate lying outside its own confidence interval. time_markers: the infiltrate was scored on H&E and explicitly includes lymphocytes, plasma cells, granulocytes and macrophages, so it was coded as other_immune rather than TIL. hpv_positive_pct=52 refers to high-risk HPV by LCD-array (31/60); including low-risk types it is 33/60 (55%), and p16 was positive in 31/60 (52%) but the concordance between p16 and HPV DNA is not reported. No immunotherapy was administered, so key_finding_immunotherapy=NA and the authors' PD-L1 rationale is recorded under other_key_outcomes.

title: Prognostic Role of PD-L1 in Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

country_setting: NA
funding: None disclosed
conflicts_of_interest: none declared (per Disclosures statement)

key_finding_prognosis: NR

other_key_outcomes: Largest pooled meta-analysis to date: 15 studies, 1,445 patients, 10 countries. Median PD-L1 prevalence 57% (IQR 44-66%). Meta-regression: HPV adjustment strengthened the CSS association (HR 2.06, 95% CI 1.21-3.51) and fully explained observed heterogeneity (I2=0%). title: Evaluation of programmed cell death ligand 1 expression in a contemporary cohort of penile squamous cell carcinoma and its correlation with clinicopathologic and survival parameters: A study of 134 patients.

funding: NR
conflicts_of_interest: NR
population_description: 134 men with penile carcinoma treated 2009-2020, paraffin blocks available; PD-L1 (CPS), p16, p53 IHC correlated with clinicopathology and survival

primary_aim_as_stated: To analyze PD-L1 expression and its correlation with various clinicopathologic parameters and survival outcomes in a contemporary cohort of 134 patients with PC

funding: Czech Health Research Council (NU21J-03-00019); Charles University (Cooperatio Medical Diagnostics); Ministry of Health, Czech Republic (MH CZ DRO-VFN 64165); European Regional Development Fund (EF16_013/0001674, BBMRI_CZ LM2018125)
conflicts_of_interest: none declared
population_description: 152 patients with surgically resected/biopsied invasive pSCC, 2002-2022; mean age 65.52 years; analyzed for tumour budding, TILs (CD3/CD8 immunoscore + subjective brisk/non-brisk), p53, p16, MMR IHC

title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio predicts a poor prognosis for penile cancer with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.
study_design: retrospective multicentre cohort study with propensity score matching (PSM)
country_setting: China; 4 centres (SYSUCC 85.1%, ACHIGMU 7.0%, GMUCC 6.2%, FAHGMU 1.7%)
funding: GuangDong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (2024A1515013007) to Kai Yao; Beijing Xisike Clinical Oncology Research Foundation (Y-Gilead2024-ZD-0239) to Kai Yao; China Postdoctoral Science Foundation (GZB20240901, 2024M763799) to Xingliang Tan
conflicts_of_interest: None declared
population_description: 582 PSCC patients from 4 centres 2010-2023, all underwent bilateral radical inguinal lymphadenectomy with definitive pN staging; mean follow-up 41.1+/-31.4 months; 46.4% node-positive

title: Tumor-infiltrating plasma cells are a prognostic factor in penile squamous cell carcinoma.

funding: Open Access funding enabled and organised by Projekt DEAL (no separate research-funding statement found)

extraction_note: Denominators vary slightly by marker/compartment across Table 2 (87-93 analysed per marker) due to missing/erroneous TMA cores excluded per protocol; n_patients=93 refers to the full cohort (all subsequent per-marker Ns are subsets thereof, explicitly reported, not a hidden discrepancy).

title: Human papillomavirus infection affects treatment outcomes and the immune microenvironment in patients with advanced penile squamous cell carcinoma receiving programmed cell death protein 1 inhibitor-based combination therapy.
study_design: retrospective cohort study (advanced PSCC receiving PD1-inhibitor-based combination therapy); includes bulk RNA-seq substudy and an embedded meta-analysis of published HPV-associated ICI cohorts
country_setting: China (Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou)
funding: Guangdong Province Nature Foundation of China Project (2021A1515220182, 2022A1515012321, 2022A1515012200); Science and Technology Planning Project of Shenzhen Municipality (JCYJ20190807145409328); Shenzhen Science and Technology Program (RCYX20221008093032008)
conflicts_of_interest: none declared
population_description: 87 patients with stage IV/advanced PSCC treated at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (April 2019-May 2023) with PD1 inhibitor-based combination therapy (PCT); 56 HPV-negative, 31 HPV-positive
hpv_method: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) for HPV DNA (23 subtypes, high-risk and low-risk)
immunotherapy_agent: PD1 inhibitors (toripalimab, tislelizumab, camrelizumab, sintilimab) plus chemotherapy +/- anti-EGFR (nimotuzumab)
primary_aim_as_stated: To investigate the predictive value of HPV status regarding treatment efficacy and disease prognosis in patients with advanced PSCC receiving PD1 inhibitor-based combination therapy, and to explore differences in the immune microenvironment between HPV+ and HPV- PSCC tissues
key_finding_time: RNA-seq/CIBERSORT showed HPV+ tumors trended toward higher proportions of tumor-killing immune subtypes (CD8+ T cells, activated memory CD4+ T cells, M1 macrophages) and lower tumor-promoting subtypes (resting memory CD4+ T cells, M2 macrophages); TIDE score was significantly lower in HPV+ group (p=.016), suggesting less immunosuppression
key_finding_hpv: HPV+ status associated with significantly better ORR (91.7% vs 64.6%, p=.014) and DCR (100% vs 79.2%, p=.025) in first-line PCT; superior PFS (p=.005) and OS (p=.004). Benefits not observed in multi-line PCT. HPV remained independent predictor of ORR (OR 6.697, p=.024), PFS (HR 0.172, p=.002), and OS (HR 0.087, p=.020) on multivariate analysis
key_finding_prognosis: Landmark analyses: HPV+ superiority in PFS visible within 3 months, strengthening through 12 months; OS superiority emerged later, within 9 and 12 months. Embedded meta-analysis of 6 studies (635 patients, HPV-associated cancers on ICI) confirmed HPV+ associated with better ORR (OR 1.82, p=.006) and 12-month PFS (OR 6.81, p=.0003)
key_finding_immunotherapy: HPV positivity is proposed as a predictive biomarker for response to PD1-inhibitor-based combination therapy in PSCC; effect attributed to HPV-induced antitumor immune activation (RAGE, PI3K/AKT pathways; higher CD8+ T-cell proportion) synergizing with chemotherapy/anti-EGFR-induced immune infiltration
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective design with possible incomplete/inaccurate data; smaller patient numbers particularly in HPV+ and multi-line subgroups led to wide 95% CIs in multivariate analyses, warranting cautious interpretation; results reflect combination therapy (PD1 inhibitor + chemo +/- anti-EGFR) rather than ICI monotherapy specifically
other_key_outcomes: NR
extraction_note: n_patients=87 es la cohorte total (56 HPV-, 31 HPV+); el analisis principal de eficacia/sobrevida (Tablas 2-5, landmark) se restringe al subgrupo de primera linea n=76 (50 HPV-, 26 HPV+) - aclarar si se prefiere ese N. time_compartment=tumor es una simplificacion: CIBERSORT se aplico sobre RNA-seq de tejido tumoral bulk (6 HPV+ / 9 HPV- muestras), sin distincion explicita intratumoral vs estromal como en estudios de IHC. El estudio incluye un metaanalisis embebido (Figura 3) combinando su cohorte con 5 estudios publicados sobre canceres HPV-asociados tratados con ICI - se resumio en key_finding_prognosis pero no se trato como estudio separado porque el foco central del articulo es la cohorte primaria propia.

title: Immunotherapy in the Management of Penile Cancer-A Systematic Review.
study_design: systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines; search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov (last search 10 Feb 2025); 35 studies included from 320 records identified; synthesis grouped by treatment strategy (maintenance, combination, monotherapy, novel combinations)
country_setting: NA
funding: Open Access Funding by Karl Landsteiner University of Health Sciences, Krems, Austria
conflicts_of_interest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest
population_description: Systematic review synthesizing 35 studies (clinical trials and real-world/retrospective series) investigating immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced/refractory PSCC
immunotherapy_agent: Atezolizumab, avelumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab, ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, retifanlimab
primary_aim_as_stated: To synthesize current evidence on the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in PSCC, with a focus on their application in advanced and refractory settings
key_finding_time: NA
key_finding_hpv: HPV-positive status, particularly HPV16 positivity, was associated with improved ICI response (HERCULES: 55.6% response in HPV16+ tumours vs 39.4% overall cORR); PERICLES showed improved PFS in hrHPV-positive tumours (p=0.003); PD-L1 expression was more frequent in HPV-negative tumours, attributed to higher tumour mutational burden and chronic inflammation
key_finding_prognosis: High PD-L1 expression (up to 79% of primary/metastatic PSCC) was associated with poor prognosis, particularly in HPV-negative tumours, while separately being predictive of ICI efficacy
key_finding_immunotherapy: Across trials (Table 3): HERCULES (pembrolizumab+chemo, first-line) cORR 39.4%, mOS 9.6mo; PERICLES (atezolizumab+/-RT) missed primary endpoint (1-yr PFS 12.5% vs 35% target), mOS 11.3mo; AcSe (nivolumab monotherapy, post-chemo) ORR 14%, mOS 8.5mo; ORPHEUS (retifanlimab, first-line) ORR 16.7%, mOS 7.2mo; PULSE (avelumab maintenance) PFS 63.5% at 12mo. Real-world data: El Zarif et al. (n=92) ORR 13%; Zhuang et al. (n=21) mOS 8.2mo, NLR associated with worse outcomes; Rouvinov et al. (n=3, cemiplimab first-line) near-complete response in all three
limitations_as_stated: Evidence remains sparse, limited to small cohorts and case reports; PSCC rarity precludes large-scale prospective trials; heterogeneity of study designs and treatment settings across included studies; no dedicated neoadjuvant ICI trials in PSCC to date
other_key_outcomes: MSI-High/TMB-High status present in ~1% of PSCC cases is associated with durable ICI response; ESMO guidelines recommend ICI consideration for MSI-High/TMB-High PSCC resistant to standard therapy; PRISMA flow: 320 records identified -> 35 studies included (Fig 1); centralization of care (EAU-ASCO 2024) and InPACT trial highlighted as infrastructure for future ICI trials in PSCC
extraction_note: Distinguishable from refs 19/20 (both meta-analyses with pooled quantitative synthesis) -- this is a narrative systematic review with no forest plots or pooled effect estimates, so publication_type=systematic_review is unambiguous here. immunotherapy_setting coded as advanced as a pragmatic single-value summary since all reported trial/real-world data are in advanced/metastatic/refractory disease; the review's discussion of neoadjuvant potential (Sec 4.3) is prospective/aspirational, not extracted data. time_compartment left NR rather than tumor because only one cited primary study (PERICLES) specifies a compartment, and generalizing it to the whole review would overstate consistency.

title: Final Results From a Phase I Trial and Expansion Cohorts of Cabozantinib and Nivolumab Alone or With Ipilimumab for Advanced/Metastatic Genitourinary Tumors.
study_design: investigator-initiated, multicenter, phase I trial with dose-escalation plus seven expansion cohorts (CaboNivo doublet: UC, ccRCC, adenocarcinoma of bladder/urachal; CaboNivoIpi triplet: UC, ccRCC, penile cancer, squamous cell carcinoma of bladder/other rare GU tumors)
country_setting: United States; 6 institutions (multicentre)
funding: Supported by the National Cancer Institute Intramural Program and the Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program
conflicts_of_interest: Extensive individual author disclosures (consulting, research funding, employment, stock ownership across numerous pharma companies); several authors reported no conflicts
population_description: Multi-tumor basket phase I trial, N=120 total enrolled (2015-2020, median follow-up 49.2 months); penile squamous cell carcinoma subgroup: 11 patients enrolled, all in the CaboNivoIpi (triplet) expansion cohort only, 9 evaluable for response
time_markers: PD-1, CD8, CTLA-4, TIM-3, Treg, other_immune
immunotherapy_agent: Cabozantinib (multi-kinase inhibitor) + nivolumab (anti-PD-1) + ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4) -- triplet (CaboNivoIpi); penile cohort received only this triplet regimen, not the CaboNivo doublet
primary_aim_as_stated: To evaluate the final safety, overall response rate, progression-free survival and overall survival of CaboNivo and CaboNivoIpi in patients with advanced/metastatic genitourinary tumors (phase I dose-escalation plus seven expansion cohorts), with exploratory peripheral immune-subset and cytokine correlates
key_finding_time: NA
key_finding_hpv: NA
key_finding_prognosis: NA
key_finding_immunotherapy: In the penile carcinoma cohort (n=9 evaluable, all CaboNivoIpi), ORR was 44.4% (4/9 PR, 0 CR), disease control rate 100%; median PFS 4.8 months (95% CI 3.1-6.4), median OS 6.7 months (95% CI 5.2-23.9). Trial-wide (N=108 evaluable): overall ORR 38.0% (CR 11.1%); grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 84% (CaboNivo) and 80% (CaboNivoIpi) of patients
limitations_as_stated: Lack of randomisation between CaboNivo and CaboNivoIpi arms; small sample size limits between-treatment comparisons, especially for small per-histology cohorts like penile (n=9); lack of tumour-tissue profiling of T cells/MDSCs in the TME (only peripheral blood assessed); heterogeneity across different GU malignancies in the immune correlative analyses limits interpretation and warrants a more streamlined approach
other_key_outcomes: Trial-wide: 120 patients enrolled, median follow-up 49.2 months; ORR 38% (CR 11.1%), DCR 81.5%; ITT median OS 15.5 months, median PFS 5.5 months. CaboNivo ORR 44.1% vs CaboNivoIpi 30.6% (non-randomised comparison). Peripheral correlates (pooled across all tumour types, not penile-specific): myeloid cells (M-MDSC, classical monocytes, DCs) decreased with both regimens; activated proliferative T cells (Ki-67+HLA-DR+/ICOS+/GITR+) increased more with CaboNivoIpi but survival association seen mainly in the CaboNivo arm; elevated baseline PlGF and TNF-alpha associated with worse PFS/OS
extraction_note: Multi-tumour basket phase I trial; PSCC is one of several rare GU histologies, present only in the CaboNivoIpi triplet expansion (all 11 penile patients received cabozantinib+nivolumab+ipilimumab; none received the CaboNivo doublet). n_patients=11 is total penile patients enrolled (Table 1); 9 were evaluable for response (Table 2), the denominator for the efficacy figures recorded here. The extensive peripheral-blood immune-subset and cytokine correlative analyses (Figs 3, A3-A11) were performed on the pooled cohort across all tumour histologies and are never broken down by tumour type, so none of it can be attributed specifically to the penile subgroup -- this is why key_finding_time/hpv/prognosis are NA rather than populated from those figures. time_compartment is NR rather than a tumour/stroma value because the correlates are peripheral-blood-based, a limitation the authors themselves flag in the Discussion.

title: Efficacy of pembrolizumab and vorinostat combination in patients with recurrent and/or metastatic squamous cell carcinomas: a phase 2 basket trial.
study_design: open-label, nonrandomized, multicenter, basket phase 2 trial
country_setting: France (multicentre, sponsor Unicancer); described as conducted in Europe; number of recruiting centres NR
funding: EraPerMed ERAPERMED2018-078-PEVOdata (ANR-18-PERM-0010); Luxembourg National Research Fund; Fondation ARC; Unicancer (sponsor); Italian Ministry of Health; EU Horizon 2020 MSCA 847718
conflicts_of_interest: Extensive; multiple authors report honoraria/advisory roles (MSD, BMS, AstraZeneca, Roche and others); remaining authors declare none
population_description: Adults with recurrent and/or metastatic SCC (head and neck, cervix, anus, vulva/vagina, penis, lung), ICI-naive, ECOG 0-1; penile cohort n=11, all male, median age 71 (range 39-82)
hpv_method: p16 IHC plus HPV PCR typing (real-time SYBR Green PCR for HPV16/18/33; GP5+/GP6+ consensus PCR with Sanger sequencing on negatives)
immunotherapy_agent: pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w plus vorinostat 400 mg PO once daily
primary_aim_as_stated: To evaluate the antitumor activity of pembrolizumab combined with vorinostat in recurrent/metastatic SCC of head and neck, cervix, lung, anus, vulva/vagina and penis, using ORR by investigator assessment as primary endpoint
key_finding_time: PD-L1 CPS positively associated with ORR (5.6% for CPS=0 vs 30% for CPS>=1, P=0.04; up to 45% at CPS>=20); no association between ORR and TPS. Whole-trial analysis, not penile-specific
key_finding_hpv: HPV-positive patients had higher ORR than HPV-negative (34% vs 16%, P=0.03), longer OS (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.27-0.73) and PFS (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.36-0.84). Pooled across all SCC sites; no HPV-stratified analysis within the penile cohort
key_finding_prognosis: High TMB associated with lower risk of death (OS HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05-0.79) and progression (PFS HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93); TP53 alterations associated with worse OS, PIK3CA with longer OS
key_finding_immunotherapy: Penile cohort did not meet its primary endpoint: ORR 18% (2/11 PR, 95% CI 2.3-52), median DOR 1.1 months, median PFS 2.4 months (95% CI 0.5-4.1), median OS 4.4 months (95% CI 1.6-11.0), the shortest OS of the six cohorts. Overall ORR 26%
limitations_as_stated: Basket design with several small cohorts limits power; penile and vulvar/vaginal cohorts particularly small; no designated control arms; univariate nature of biomarker analyses limits their predictive value; age-response association derived from subgroup analysis
other_key_outcomes: Safety: 101/111 (91%) had at least one TRAE, grade >=3 in 44.4%; vorinostat toxicity forced dose reduction or interruption in 66%. WES on 77 samples: alterations in RAD51, NOTCH1 or B2M associated with longer PFS
extraction_note: Basket trial across 6 SCC primary sites; N=11 is the penile cohort (identical in safety and per-protocol sets), not the 112 enrolled / 111 safety / 107 efficacy parent trial. hpv_positive_pct=36 is penile-specific by PCR typing (4/11, Table 1); p16 was positive in 4/8 evaluable penile cases (3 missing) and the whole-trial HPV+ rate was 57%. All HPV, PD-L1 and TMB outcome analyses are pooled across SCC sites; no penile-specific biomarker analysis is reported. time_compartment coded both because CPS counts tumour cells plus lymphocytes and macrophages, but no tumour-vs-stroma separation is reported. Ethics committee named in Methods (National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition) is inconsistent with the French/European regulatory framework described in the same paragraph

title: Pembrolizumab Plus Platinum-Based Chemotherapy for Patients With Advanced Penile Cancer: The Nonrandomized HERCULES (LACOG 0218) Clinical Trial.
study_design: phase 2 single-arm nonrandomized clinical trial evaluating first-line pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy (cisplatin/carboplatin + fluorouracil) in 11 Brazilian centres
country_setting: Brazil; 11 centres
funding: Merck Sharp & Dohme, LLC, a subsidiary of Merck & Co, Inc; supplied study drugs and provided funding for conducting the trial
conflicts_of_interest: Extensive individual disclosures; Cotait Maluf reports grants from Merck Sharp & Dohme during the conduct of the study plus consulting/advisory/research funding from multiple other pharma companies outside the submitted work; several co-authors report similar industry relationships; some authors report no disclosures
population_description: Patients with advanced (metastatic, recurrent, or locally advanced not amenable to curative-intent therapy) PSCC receiving first-line pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy, enrolled Aug 2020-Dec 2022 at 11 Brazilian sites; median age 55.8 years (range 30.2-75.5); 64.9% metastatic, 21.6% recurrent, 13.5% locally advanced
immunotherapy_agent: Pembrolizumab plus cisplatin (or carboplatin) plus fluorouracil
primary_aim_as_stated: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of adding an immune checkpoint inhibitor to chemotherapy for advanced PSCC
key_finding_time: NA
key_finding_hpv: HPV16-positive patients showed higher ORR (55.6%, 95% CI 21.2-86.3) and longer PFS (7.6 months) than HPV16-negative patients (35% ORR, 5.6 months PFS); no ORR difference between PD-L1-negative and PD-L1-positive patients (66.7% CPS0 vs 33.3% CPS>=1); TMB-high patients had higher ORR (75%) than TMB-low (36.4%)
key_finding_prognosis: NA
key_finding_immunotherapy: ORR by investigator assessment 39.4% (95% CI 22.9-57.9) among 33 efficacy-evaluable patients; ORR by central review 42.4% (95% CI 25.5-60.8); clinical benefit rate 45.5%; median PFS 5.4 months (95% CI 2.7-7.2); median OS 9.6 months (95% CI 6.4-13.2); 6-month, 12-month and 24-month OS of 69.7%, 41.4% and 19.4%
limitations_as_stated: Single-arm study without a randomized active comparator, challenging to conduct given disease rarity; small sample size did not allow statistically powered exploratory biomarker analysis; trial assessed addition of ICI to doublet chemotherapy, which might not reflect clinical practice for fit and younger patients where triplet chemotherapy regimens are used despite higher toxicity
other_key_outcomes: Treatment-related AEs of any grade in 91.9% of 37 treated patients, grade 3-4 in 51.4%; immune-related AEs any grade 21.6%, grade 3-4 5.4%; no treatment-related deaths; NGS performed in 35/37 (94.6%), median 3 clinically relevant alterations, most frequent TP53 (57.1%), CDKN2A (51.4%), TERT (31.4%), FAT1 (22.9%), NOTCH1 (20.0%); HRQoL improved from baseline to week 24 in global health status and all functional scales, with improvement also in pain and insomnia symptom scales
extraction_note: n_patients ambiguous within the source: 37 enrolled/treated is the safety analysis and the denominator for the exploratory biomarker table (PD-L1, HPV16, TMB, p16), while efficacy outcomes (ORR, PFS, OS, Table 2) rest on the 33 patients eligible for efficacy analysis (4 excluded for major protocol violations). Recorded 37 because it is the denominator underlying the HPV/PD-L1/TMB biomarker findings most relevant to this synthesis; flagging that 33 may be preferred for the efficacy-outcome fields specifically. hpv_method recorded as NR because the article states biomarker methodologies are in Supplement 3, which was not provided in the PDF furnished for extraction. time_compartment=both follows the same PD-L1 CPS-definition convention used elsewhere in this set (CPS = staining tumour cells + lymphocytes + macrophages / total viable tumour cells).

title: Neoadjuvant and/or adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors combined with chemotherapy for locally advanced resectable penile squamous cell carcinoma.
study_design: prospective, non-randomized, two-cohort phase II trial (ChiCTR2400094629) of sintilimab plus TP (nab-paclitaxel + cisplatin) chemotherapy as neoadjuvant-adjuvant or adjuvant-only perioperative therapy, assignment by preoperative resectability criteria
country_setting: China; 2 centres (Tianjin First Central Hospital; Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital)
funding: Natural Science Foundation of Tianjin (23JCZDJC00340); National Natural Science Foundation of China (82402166); Tianjin Key Medical Discipline Construction Project (TJYXZDXK-3-003A)
conflicts_of_interest: None declared; authors state the work was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest
population_description: Locally advanced resectable PSCC with N2 (64.0%) or N3 (36.0%) nodal disease, ECOG 0-1, median age 55 years, treated May 2022-Dec 2024 at 2 centres; 18 assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant pathway and 7 to adjuvant-only pathway based on preoperative resectability criteria
immunotherapy_agent: Sintilimab plus nab-paclitaxel plus cisplatin (TP regimen)
primary_aim_as_stated: To investigate the efficacy (primary endpoint progression-free survival) and safety of sintilimab combined with chemotherapy as a neoadjuvant and/or adjuvant therapy for patients with locally advanced PSCC
key_finding_time: NA
key_finding_hpv: Non-significant trend toward improved PFS in p16-positive tumours compared with p16-negative tumours (P=0.116, HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.03-1.85)
key_finding_prognosis: NA
key_finding_immunotherapy: Among 17 neoadjuvant-evaluable patients: ORR 52.9% (2 CR, 7 PR), DCR 76.5%; treatment-naive subgroup ORR 66.7% (8/12); of 12 patients who underwent surgery, 2/12 (16.7%) achieved pCR and 3/12 (25%) achieved MPR; 18-month PFS and OS for entire cohort 71.4% and 90.0%; patients achieving radiological CR/PR after neoadjuvant therapy had significantly better PFS than those with SD/PD (P=0.005, HR 0.07, 95% CI 0.01-0.46); PD-L1 expression (CPS>=20 vs <20) not significantly associated with PFS (P=0.951, HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.14-7.16)
limitations_as_stated: Non-randomized two-cohort design introduced selection bias, reflected in higher baseline tumour burden in patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy (a reflection of real-world clinical triage rather than randomization); small sample size restricts interpretation and the specific contribution of immunotherapy remains uncertain despite the correlation between clinical response and PFS; subgroup analyses (PD-L1, p16) are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts; multivariable analysis not conducted given limited sample size
other_key_outcomes: Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs in 5 patients (20%): anemia, neutropenia, arthralgia and rash; most common any-grade AEs alopecia (52.0%) and peripheral sensory neuropathy (48.0%); no treatment-related deaths; individual trajectories reported, e.g. Patient #25 (neoadjuvant-adjuvant, longest PFS 34.7 months) and Patient #18 (77% tumour reduction after neoadjuvant therapy, declined surgery, PFS 15.2 months at last assessment); study is ongoing with planned enrolment of 28 patients (26 enrolled at data cutoff, 1 withdrew consent before treatment)
extraction_note: n_patients is internally inconsistent in the source: Abstract and Section 3.1 state 25 patients comprised the safety and efficacy analysis populations, but Table 3 headers the same survival outcomes as 'Overall cohort (N=24)' and the CONSORT diagram (Figure 1) states '25 Analyzed for safety' vs '24 Analyzed for efficacy'. Recorded 25 per the Abstract/Section 3.1 statement; flagging the N=24 alternative used for the Table 3 survival figures. immunotherapy_setting has no controlled token for a combined neoadjuvant-plus-adjuvant design in which a subset (7/25) received adjuvant-only therapy and never got neoadjuvant ICI; coded as neoadjuvant as the closest single-value fit, reflecting the majority pathway (18/25) and the trial's stated focus. hpv_method recorded as p16 IHC specifically (not molecular HPV testing) because that is the only marker the article names ('P16 IHC (n=19)', Table 1); no PCR/ISH confirmation is reported. This is a preliminary analysis of an ongoing trial, not a final report.

title: Immune checkpoint blockade with anti-programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) monoclonal antibody (mAb) cemiplimab: ongoing and future perspectives in rare genital cancers treatment.
study_design: narrative commentary/perspective synthesizing case reports and small trials of cemiplimab (and other anti-PD-1 agents) in penile and vulvar SCC, extrapolating rationale from cervical SCC; no primary PSCC cohort of its own
country_setting: NA
funding: None declared; authors state no specific grant was received for this research from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors
conflicts_of_interest: No competing interests declared
population_description: No primary cohort; synthesizes locally advanced/metastatic penile and vulvar SCC patients drawn from cited case reports and small trials (phase II basket study NCT02721732, AcSe nivolumab trial, YBL-006 phase I, CheckMate 358, KEYNOTE-158, and three individual cemiplimab case reports)
immunotherapy_agent: Cemiplimab (primary focus); pembrolizumab and nivolumab discussed as comparators
primary_aim_as_stated: To review the current and future role of cemiplimab in rare genital cancers (penile and vulvar SCC), given the molecular and viral similarities with HPV-driven cervical SCC
key_finding_time: NA
key_finding_hpv: HPV-positive penile SCC associated with better survival (93%) and greater radiosensitivity than HPV-negative tumours; HPV16/18 implicated in up to 50% of penile SCC; HPV-positive tumours described as more susceptible to immunotherapy via effector T-cell modulation, with increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration reported in HPV-positive head and neck SCC (extrapolated, not penile-specific data); high PD-L1 expression noted to correlate with an unfavourable outcome in penile and vulvar SCC, contrasting with its predictive role in other tumour types
key_finding_prognosis: NA
key_finding_immunotherapy: AcSe nivolumab trial (largest prospective anti-PD-1 study in penile SCC to date): ORR 14%, median OS 8.5 months; phase II basket study NCT02721732: 3 penile SCC patients treated with pembrolizumab after platinum-based triplet, objective durable response only in the patient with a microsatellite-instability-high tumour; YBL-006 phase I: 1 complete response among 10 radiologically evaluable patients, occurring in a penile SCC patient; three individual case reports of metastatic penile SCC achieving complete or outstanding response to cemiplimab; EMPOWER-Cervical 1 (cervical cancer, not penile) cited as rationale: median OS 12 vs 8.8 months (HR 0.69) overall and 11.1 vs 8.8 months (HR 0.73) in the SCC subgroup favouring cemiplimab over chemotherapy; no dedicated cemiplimab trial in penile SCC exists to date
limitations_as_stated: No prospective data distinguish tumours originating in penile/vulvar skin from those in mucosal or glans epithelium; complexity of immune activation and variability in tumour biology across patients make biomarker identification difficult; PD-L1 and TMB are not established as predictive biomarkers in genital SCC (per EMPOWER-CSCC-1 correlative results); evidence base is largely limited to case reports and small cohorts
other_key_outcomes: Table 1 lists ongoing cemiplimab combination trials in advanced solid tumours (with anti-TGF-beta mAb, TLR9 agonists, an EGFR/CD28 bispecific antibody, anti-LAG3 mAb, an mRNA cytokine mixture, and chemotherapy combinations); none specific to PSCC. Authors suggest exploring EZH2 inhibition as a future strategy to circumvent anti-PD-1 resistance, based on head and neck SCC data
extraction_note: This reference is not among the reviews the HANDOFF flags as MMAT-exempt (refs 19/20/28); the validation script will likely raise a WARN for relation_type=review outside that set. Kept as review/narrative_review deliberately because the piece is structurally a narrative commentary with no primary PSCC data of its own -- coding it as original_research would misrepresent it. hpv_stratified/hpv_positive_pct recorded as NR rather than a computed figure because, unlike refs 19/20, this piece performs no quantitative pooling of its own; background HPV prevalence figures cited (e.g. 'up to 50% of penile SCCs') are general-literature statements, not a stratified analysis of an included patient set.
